subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up
messages:
From: marissa.co@redwood-inference.com
To: Emma Stone <emma@finlytics.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com, neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Hi Emma — thank you again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short pilot.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary workload: structured transaction classification + enrichment (JSON outputs, fixed schema) for Payment & KYC flows.
- Volume: ~300k inference calls/month, bursty daytime traffic.
- Quality bar: schema-complete responses with "transaction_id" and "status" required; acceptable fallback is structured error object.

Recommended initial model variants to evaluate (based on the prompts you shared):
- redwood-4b-q (quantized) — fastest and cheapest; good baseline for throughput and initial schema compliance testing.
- redwood-13b (fp16) — stronger on schema adherence and complex extraction; higher token cost but better JSON-field coverage in our evals.

What we ran so far (attached): benchmark_results_q3.csv and a short eval summary (link below). High-level numbers from our internal fit tests using your sample prompt set:
- redwood-4b-q: JSON schema pass rate ~92% (missing optional fields most common).
- redwood-13b: JSON schema pass rate ~97%; fewer retries required.

Tool/function-calling notes:
- With function-calling + strict JSON schema enforcement, we can validate output and either request a retry (up to N times) or fallback to a structured error response. In our Q3 suite we saw ~4% of calls requiring a single retry on 13b, ~8% on 4b-q.
- We can instrument deterministic retries/backoff (configurable per-route) and automatic fallback to a lighter model if latency SLOs are at risk.

Attachments we uploaded to the Drive folder: finlytics_prompt_set_v1.json (subset of prompts), schema_examples.md (expected schema + examples).

Proposed next steps:
1) You upload ~1k representative prompts (anonymized) to the Drive folder linked below.
2) Redwood runs a 72-hour pilot evaluating redwood-4b-q and redwood-13b with function-calling enabled; we’ll produce per-route pass rates, latency distributions (p50/p95), and cost estimates.
3) Tech deep-dive with Rishi & Neha (30–45 min) — proposed slots Tue 10/20 or Wed 10/21.

Can you confirm the Drive upload and which time works best for the deep-dive? Once confirmed, I’ll schedule and kick off the pilot.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood-inference.com

From: Emma Stone <emma@finlytics.ai>
To: marissa.co@redwood-inference.com
Cc: platform@finlytics.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Hi Marissa — really helpful recap, thanks. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we upload more data: 

1) Latency: What p95 should we expect for redwood-13b and redwood-4b-q with our throughput? We need to keep API response time under 500ms for enrichment calls.
2) Cost: ballpark cost per 1k tokens for each variant (pilot estimate) so I can budget internally.
3) Strict schema enforcement: can Redwood guarantee the model will not emit freeform text outside the schema if function-calling is used? We need to avoid downstream parsing errors.
4) Compliance: is there any additional info we should pass to our security team (SOC2 artefacts, data residency options) to speed procurement?

We’ll plan to upload an anonymized set of 1k prompts today unless you advise otherwise. Tue 10/20 11am PT works for the deep-dive.

Best,
Emma Stone
Head of Data Platform, FinLytics
emma@finlytics.ai

From: marissa.co@redwood-inference.com
To: Emma Stone <emma@finlytics.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com, neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-10-18T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling follow-up

Thanks Emma — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Latency (pilot conditions):
- redwood-4b-q: p50 ~40–60ms, p95 ~140–200ms for single-token latency on our dedicated pool; end-to-end (complete response) will depend on response length but should be well under your 500ms SLO for typical enrichment calls.
- redwood-13b: p50 ~80–120ms, p95 ~180–300ms in our tests. We can provision dedicated capacity to tighten p95 if you need stricter SLOs.

2) Cost (very rough pilot estimates):
- redwood-4b-q: ~$0.20 per 1k tokens
- redwood-13b (fp16): ~$1.10 per 1k tokens
Final quoted pricing will depend on committed volume and dedicated vs hosted.

3) Strict schema enforcement: function-calling with strict JSON schema + our post-validate step enforces structure. If the model output fails validation we can: 1) auto-retry with a different temperature and last-turn prompt hint, 2) fall back to a structured error object, or 3) route to the heavyweight model (13b) for a second attempt. We cannot 100% prevent creative text in the token stream at the model level, but with function-calling + validation we can ensure downstream systems only receive schema-compliant payloads.

4) Compliance artefacts: I’ll share a SOC 2 evidence pack link in the drive and loop in our security lead if they need a short call. For procurement, note that Dedicated and Private deployment options are available if you require data residency or an on-prem install.

Actions I’ll take now:
- Kick off a 72-hour pilot on redwood-4b-q and redwood-13b once you confirm the Drive upload (I created finlytics_prompt_set_v1.json in the folder as a placeholder).
- Share schema_examples.md showing enforcement, example retries, and fallback patterns.

You confirmed Tue 10/20 11am PT for the technical deep-dive — I’ll send a calendar invite to you and the platform team.

Thanks —
Marissa
